text:
Predicates:
Deadly(x) ::: x is a deadly disease.
LowSurvivalRate(x) ::: x comes with a low survival rate.
Severe(x) ::: x is a severe cancer.
BileDuctCancer(x) ::: x is bile duct cancer.
Cholangiocarcinoma(x) ::: x is a Cholangiocarcinoma.
MildFlu(x) ::: x is a mild flu.
ColorectalCancer(x) ::: x is a colorectal cancer.
Premises:
∀x (Deadly(x) → LowSurvivalRate(x)) ::: If something is a deadly disease, then it comes with a low survival rate.
∀x (Severe(x) → Deadly(x)) ::: Severe cancers are deadly diseases.
∀x (BileDuctCancer(x) → Severe(x)) ::: Bile duct cancer is a severe form of cancer.
∀x (Cholangiocarcinoma(x) → BileDuctCancer(x)) ::: All Cholangiocarcinoma is bile duct cancer.
MildFlu(x) → LowSurvivalRate(x) ::: Mild flu comes with a low survival rate.
¬(ColorectalCancer(x) ∧ BileDuctCancer(x) ∧ LowSurvivalRate(x)) ::: Colorectal cancer is not both a bile duct cancer and with a low survival rate.
Conclusion:
(ColorectalCancer(x) ∧ (MildFlu(x) ∨ BileDuctCancer(x))) ∨ (ColorectalCancer(x) ∧ MildFlu(x) ∧ BileDuctCancer(x)) ::: Colorectal cancer is a form of Cholangiocarcinoma and it is a kind of mild flu or a kind of bile duct cancer, or all of the above.
